properties.text: The encode_receipt function must map every valid transaction type to exactly one receipt prefix byte: AccessListTransaction -> 0x01, FeeMarketTransaction -> 0x02, BlobTransaction -> 0x03, SetCodeTransaction -> 0x04, LegacyTransaction -> no prefix (raw receipt). No transaction type may produce an ambiguous or missing encoding path.

reachability.notes: An attacker submits a transaction of a specific type; the encode_receipt path is determined by the isinstance checks on the transaction object. If a new transaction type is introduced without updating encode_receipt, receipts will be incorrectly encoded, causing consensus divergence across all clients.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect receipt encoding causes receipt root divergence, which is a network-wide consensus failure. All nodes that compute the receipt root differently will fork.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a transaction that causes encode_receipt to produce an incorrect prefix byte or reach an unhandled code path. Must show receipt root divergence between at least two client implementations.

properties.text: The isinstance checks in encode_receipt must be mutually exclusive: for any transaction object tx, exactly one of the five isinstance branches (AccessListTransaction, FeeMarketTransaction, BlobTransaction, SetCodeTransaction, LegacyTransaction) must match. If transaction type classes share inheritance relationships, the check order must guarantee the most specific type is matched first.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits a transaction whose type could match multiple isinstance checks due to class hierarchy. If SetCodeTransaction is a subclass of FeeMarketTransaction, the check order determines the encoding prefix.

properties.severity_justification: isinstance ambiguity in encode_receipt would produce incorrect prefix byte, causing receipt root divergence and network-wide consensus split between clients with different check ordering.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a transaction type that triggers the wrong isinstance branch due to inheritance, leading to incorrect receipt encoding. Reference stride-016.

properties.text: The decode_receipt function must reject any receipt byte array whose first byte is not in the set {1, 2, 3, 4} by raising an explicit exception (not via Python assert). This validation must not be bypassable via Python optimization flags (-O).

reachability.notes: Attacker on P2P network sends receipt bytes with an arbitrary first byte. The current implementation uses an assert statement, which can be disabled in Python's optimized mode (-O). If assertions are disabled, any byte value passes the check.

properties.severity_justification: If assertions are disabled in production, arbitrary receipt type prefixes would be accepted, allowing malformed receipts to be decoded and potentially causing consensus splits or RLP decoder exploitation. Reference stride-015.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that running the execution client with Python -O flag allows receipts with invalid type prefixes to be decoded. Must show the assert is the sole guard.

properties.text: For any receipt byte array with first byte b where b in {1, 2, 3, 4}, decode_receipt must strip exactly the first byte and pass the remaining bytes receipt[1:] to rlp.decode_to(Receipt, ...). The decoded Receipt object must have all fields (succeeded, cumulative_gas_used, bloom, logs) well-formed.

reachability.notes: Attacker crafts receipt bytes with a valid prefix but malformed RLP payload after the prefix byte. The sliced bytes receipt[1:] are passed directly to the RLP decoder.

properties.severity_justification: Malformed RLP after a valid type prefix could crash the RLP decoder, produce inconsistent Receipt objects, or trigger bugs that differ across client implementations, causing consensus splits. Reference stride-001.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must craft receipt bytes with valid prefix (1-4) followed by malformed RLP that causes decoder crash, panic, or produces an unexpected Receipt object.

properties.text: If the input to decode_receipt is not of type Bytes (i.e., it is already a Receipt object), the function must return it unchanged without any transformation or decoding.

reachability.notes: This path handles already-decoded Receipt objects passed internally. No external entry point can directly trigger this path with attacker-controlled data.

properties.severity_justification: Only affects internal code paths where receipts are already decoded. Incorrect handling would be a logic bug but not externally exploitable.

properties.text: Legacy transaction receipts must be returned by encode_receipt without any type prefix byte or additional RLP wrapping. The raw Receipt object must be returned as-is. This encoding asymmetry must be consistently implemented across all client implementations.

reachability.notes: An attacker submits a LegacyTransaction. If one client RLP-wraps the receipt while another returns it raw, the receipt roots will diverge, causing a consensus split.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent legacy receipt encoding across clients would cause receipt root divergence and a network-wide consensus split. This is the most subtle encoding edge case.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate that a LegacyTransaction causes different receipt encoding across two client implementations, leading to receipt root mismatch.

properties.text: The encode_receipt and decode_receipt functions must be inverses for typed transactions: for any transaction tx of type T in {AccessList, FeeMarket, Blob, SetCode} and its receipt r, decode_receipt(encode_receipt(tx, r)) must produce an object equal to r.

reachability.notes: Any transaction submitted by an attacker triggers the encode path during execution and the decode path during block import. If these are not inverses, receipt verification fails.

properties.severity_justification: Encode/decode asymmetry would cause blocks to fail receipt root verification on re-import, potentially causing nodes to reject valid blocks or accept invalid ones.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a receipt that round-trips differently through encode then decode, producing a different receipt root.

properties.text: Block headers must be immutable after freeze(Header) is called. No field of a Header object may be modified after the slotted_freezable freeze operation completes. Any attempt to mutate a frozen Header must raise an exception.

reachability.notes: An attacker sends a block via P2P that is deserialized into a Header. If the freeze mechanism can be bypassed (e.g., via Python runtime tricks), the header could be mutated after construction, changing its hash.

properties.severity_justification: Header mutability after freeze would allow header hash inconsistency, potentially causing fork choice errors and consensus failures.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate mutation of a frozen Header object and show that the header hash changes, causing validation inconsistency.

properties.text: All 21 header fields must be explicitly set during Header construction before freeze() is called. No field may retain a default or zero value unless that is its specified valid value (e.g., difficulty=0 in PoS). The construction order must enforce that all fields are assigned.

reachability.notes: A block proposer or the execution engine constructs headers. If the slotted_freezable pattern does not enforce complete field assignment, a header with missing fields could be created and propagated.

properties.severity_justification: Partial header construction could produce blocks with zero or default values for critical fields like base_fee_per_gas or requests_hash, which would cause validation failures or consensus divergence. Reference stride-014.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires internal caller to construct a partial header. Not directly reachable from external entry points.

properties.text: In post-merge Osaka fork, the Header difficulty field must be 0 and nonce must be bytes8(0x0000000000000000). Any block with non-zero difficulty or non-zero nonce must be rejected during validation.

reachability.notes: An attacker crafts a block with non-zero difficulty or nonce. If validation is missing, the block is accepted, potentially causing consensus splits between clients that validate vs. ignore these fields. Reference stride-010.

properties.severity_justification: Non-zero PoW fields in PoS blocks could smuggle data, cause consensus splits between validating and non-validating clients, or be misinterpreted by legacy code paths.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must craft a block with non-zero difficulty/nonce and show it is accepted by at least one client implementation that fails to validate these fields.

properties.text: In post-merge Osaka fork, the Header ommers_hash must always equal EMPTY_OMMER_HASH (keccak256(rlp([]))). Any block with a different ommers_hash must be rejected during validation.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends a block with non-empty ommers_hash. If the ommers_hash check is missing, the block could carry hidden data in the ommers field.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect ommers_hash in PoS could cause consensus splits between clients that validate vs. skip this field. Also enables data smuggling through ommer headers.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with non-EMPTY_OMMER_HASH being accepted by a client that fails to validate this field.

properties.text: The ommers tuple in a Block must always be empty (length 0) in PoS forks. Any block containing non-empty ommers must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block with non-empty ommers tuple via P2P. Must be rejected to prevent data smuggling and inconsistent state.

properties.severity_justification: Non-empty ommers in PoS could carry arbitrary header data and cause consensus inconsistency between clients with different validation strictness.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must craft a block with non-empty ommers and show acceptance by a client.

properties.text: The execution engine must independently compute transactions_root from the block body transactions and reject any block where the header's transactions_root does not match the computed root.

reachability.notes: Attacker constructs a block with transactions_root that does not match the actual transactions in the body. If the execution engine fails to recompute and verify, tampered transactions could be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to verify transactions_root allows an attacker to substitute transactions in a block, potentially executing unauthorized state transitions. This is a direct consensus failure.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block with mismatched transactions_root being accepted, showing that transaction substitution is possible.

properties.text: The execution engine must independently compute receipt_root from the encoded receipts of all transactions in the block and reject any block where the header's receipt_root does not match the computed root.

reachability.notes: Attacker constructs a block with mismatched receipt_root. Receipt root verification depends on correct encode_receipt behavior for all transaction types.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to verify receipt_root allows tampered receipts, which could mask failed transactions as successful or vice versa, causing incorrect state interpretation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with incorrect receipt_root being accepted, demonstrating receipt tampering.

properties.text: The execution engine must independently compute withdrawals_root from the block body withdrawals and reject any block where the header's withdrawals_root does not match the computed root.

reachability.notes: Attacker constructs a block with withdrawals_root that does not match the withdrawals in the body. If unverified, tampered withdrawals could credit incorrect addresses or amounts.

properties.severity_justification: Failure to verify withdrawals_root allows withdrawal tampering, potentially crediting ETH to attacker-controlled addresses.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate withdrawal substitution through mismatched withdrawals_root acceptance.

properties.text: The RLP decoder must safely handle all malformed inputs without panics, crashes, or undefined behavior when processing attacker-controlled receipt bytes via decode_receipt. Specifically, rlp.decode_to(Receipt, data) must either return a valid Receipt or raise a well-defined exception.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends crafted receipt bytes with valid prefix but arbitrary payload. After prefix stripping, raw bytes go directly to rlp.decode_to().

properties.severity_justification: RLP decoder crash on malformed input causes node crash, potentially enabling network-wide DoS if the malformed block propagates through P2P.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must craft receipt bytes that cause RLP decoder crash, panic, or infinite loop. Fuzz testing of rlp.decode_to() with arbitrary payloads is the recommended approach.

properties.text: The decode_receipt function must impose or rely on size limits for receipt bytes before passing them to the RLP decoder. Receipt bytes exceeding the maximum reasonable size must be rejected before RLP decoding begins.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends extremely large receipt payloads via P2P. If no size check exists before RLP decoding, memory exhaustion or CPU exhaustion is possible.

properties.severity_justification: Oversized receipts without size limits can cause memory exhaustion DoS. Impact is limited to individual nodes but could affect multiple nodes receiving the same block.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate memory or CPU exhaustion via oversized receipt bytes. Must show that EIP-7934 block size limits are insufficient to prevent this.

properties.text: A receipt decoded with type prefix b must produce the same Receipt object regardless of whether it was encoded from an AccessListTransaction (b=1), FeeMarketTransaction (b=2), BlobTransaction (b=3), or SetCodeTransaction (b=4). The prefix byte must not affect the interpretation of the RLP payload; it serves only as a type indicator for the transaction, not for the receipt contents.

reachability.notes: Attacker crafts a receipt with type prefix 0x04 (SetCode) but encodes the body as if it were for a different type. If clients check type/body consistency differently, consensus splits occur.

properties.severity_justification: Type prefix/body inconsistency in receipts could cause one client to accept and another to reject, creating a consensus split. Reference stride-005.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a receipt with mismatched type prefix and body content causing different behavior across client implementations.

properties.text: The bloom filter bytearray must be exactly 256 bytes at all times during and after add_to_bloom operations. No operation may extend or truncate the bloom filter.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits transactions that produce logs. The bloom filter is computed from these logs. If the bloom size invariant is violated, out-of-bounds access could occur.

properties.severity_justification: Bloom filter size violation would cause out-of-bounds memory access, potentially crashing the node or causing memory corruption.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a scenario where the bloom filter size changes from 256 bytes, causing out-of-bounds access.

properties.text: The bit_to_set value computed in add_to_bloom must always be in the range [0, 2047] (inclusive). The 11-bit mask 0x07FF applied to the 2-byte big-endian integer from the keccak256 hash must guarantee this bound.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls log addresses and topics which are inputs to keccak256. The bit_to_set range depends solely on the 0x07FF mask being correctly applied.

properties.severity_justification: If the 0x07FF mask is incorrectly applied, bit_to_set could exceed 2047, causing byte_index to exceed 255 and resulting in out-of-bounds bloom filter access.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate an input to add_to_bloom that causes bit_to_set to exceed 2047 due to incorrect masking.

properties.text: The byte_index computed in add_to_bloom must always be in the range [0, 255] (inclusive), ensuring all bloom filter byte accesses are within the 256-byte array bounds.

reachability.notes: Follows from PROP-0020: if bit_to_set is in [0, 2047], then bit_index is in [0, 2047], and byte_index = bit_index // 8 is in [0, 255].

properties.severity_justification: Out-of-bounds byte_index would cause bloom filter array overflow, potentially crashing the node or corrupting memory.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show byte_index exceeding 255, causing out-of-bounds access. Requires failure of the 0x07FF mask invariant.

properties.text: The add_to_bloom function must iterate exactly 3 times (at keccak256 hash byte indices 0, 2, and 4), setting exactly 3 bits per bloom entry. No fewer and no more iterations may occur.

reachability.notes: If the loop iterates a different number of times in one client vs. another, bloom filters will differ, causing receipt root divergence.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect iteration count in add_to_bloom produces a different bloom filter, causing receipt root mismatch and consensus split. Reference stride-007.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a client implementation where add_to_bloom iterates a different number of times than specified (3), causing bloom divergence.

properties.text: The keccak256 hash function used in add_to_bloom must produce at least 6 bytes of output to support 3 two-byte pair reads at indices (0,1), (2,3), and (4,5).

reachability.notes: keccak256 always produces 32 bytes. This invariant is inherently satisfied and serves as documentation.

properties.severity_justification: keccak256 always produces 32 bytes. This property is trivially satisfied and serves only as documentation of the design assumption.

properties.text: The logs_bloom function must initialize the bloom filter to all zeros (256 bytes of 0x00) before processing any logs. No pre-existing data may be present in the bloom filter.

reachability.notes: If the bloom filter is not initialized to zeros (e.g., due to memory reuse), spurious bits would cause bloom filter divergence across clients.

properties.severity_justification: Uninitialized bloom filter would contain spurious bits, causing bloom divergence and receipt root mismatch between clients, leading to consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a case where the bloom filter contains pre-existing data due to memory reuse or initialization failure.

properties.text: In logs_bloom, every log address must be added to the bloom filter exactly once via add_to_bloom(bloom, log.address). No address may be skipped or added more than once.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls which contract addresses emit logs. If any address is skipped or duplicated in bloom computation, the bloom diverges from the specification.

properties.severity_justification: Skipping or duplicating a log address in bloom computation causes bloom divergence, leading to receipt root mismatch and consensus split. Reference stride-007.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a client implementation that skips or duplicates log addresses in bloom computation, causing different bloom output.

properties.text: In logs_bloom, every topic of every log must be added to the bloom filter exactly once via add_to_bloom(bloom, topic). No topic may be skipped or added more than once.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls which topics are emitted in logs (LOG0-LOG4 opcodes). If any topic is skipped or duplicated, bloom diverges.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect topic handling in bloom computation causes bloom divergence, receipt root mismatch, and consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show topic skipping or duplication in a client's bloom computation.

properties.text: The logs_bloom function must call add_to_bloom exactly (1 + len(log.topics)) times per log entry: once for the address and once for each topic.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls log contents via contract execution. The total number of add_to_bloom calls must be deterministic for any given set of logs.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect number of add_to_bloom calls produces different bloom filter, causing receipt root divergence and consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a client calling add_to_bloom a different number of times than specified.

properties.text: The Bloom object returned by logs_bloom must be constructed from the bytearray after all logs have been processed. The Bloom must not be constructed from an intermediate state of the bytearray.

reachability.notes: This is an internal construction ordering requirement. No external entry point can trigger premature Bloom construction.

properties.severity_justification: Premature Bloom construction would produce incomplete bloom filter, but this is only possible through internal code errors.

properties.text: The bloom filter stored in a Receipt must be consistent with the logs it contains: receipt.bloom == logs_bloom(receipt.logs). Any discrepancy must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends a block with receipts whose bloom field does not match the computed logs_bloom. If this inconsistency is not detected, incorrect bloom filters propagate.

properties.severity_justification: Inconsistent bloom/logs could cause receipt root divergence if some clients verify consistency and others do not. Also impacts log query correctness.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a receipt with inconsistent bloom field being accepted by a client.

properties.text: The cumulative_gas_used field in receipts must be monotonically non-decreasing within a block. For receipts r_i and r_{i+1} at consecutive transaction indices, r_{i+1}.cumulative_gas_used >= r_i.cumulative_gas_used.

reachability.notes: Attacker submits transactions that are included in a block. The cumulative gas used in receipts must be non-decreasing. A violation indicates incorrect gas accounting.

properties.severity_justification: Violation of cumulative gas monotonicity indicates a gas accounting bug that could allow exceeding block gas limits or undercharging for execution.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block where cumulative_gas_used decreases between consecutive receipts.

properties.text: Withdrawal objects must be immutable after freeze(Withdrawal) is called. All four fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be set before freeze and cannot be modified after.

reachability.notes: Withdrawal objects are constructed from CL-provided data via Engine API. If the freeze mechanism can be bypassed, withdrawal fields could be modified after construction.

properties.severity_justification: Withdrawal mutation after freeze could alter ETH credit addresses or amounts, but requires internal caller or Engine API compromise.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Only reachable via Engine API (JWT-authenticated). Not directly attacker-controlled.

properties.text: All four Withdrawal fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) must be explicitly set during construction. A Withdrawal with missing fields must not be accepted by the execution engine.

reachability.notes: CL provides withdrawal objects via Engine API. If any field is missing or zero-valued without proper validation, incorrect ETH credits could occur.

properties.severity_justification: Incomplete withdrawal construction could credit ETH to the zero address or with zero amount, or miss crediting entirely. Requires CL bug.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires compromised or buggy CL. Not directly attacker-controlled.

properties.text: The execution layer must not independently verify withdrawal amounts or validator indices from the consensus layer. However, it must validate that the withdrawal objects are structurally well-formed (correct field types and sizes). A compromised CL sending malformed withdrawal objects must not crash the EL.

reachability.notes: A compromised CL could send inflated withdrawal amounts. The EL trusts CL withdrawal data by design. This is an architectural trust boundary.

properties.severity_justification: A compromised CL could inject withdrawals with inflated amounts, causing unauthorized ETH minting. However, this requires CL compromise which is a separate security domain.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: CL compromise is out of scope for this specific EL analysis. The trust boundary is by design.

properties.text: A compromised or buggy CL sending a withdrawal with a spoofed address must not cause the EL to credit ETH to an incorrect account beyond the intended design (where EL trusts CL withdrawal data). The Engine API JWT authentication must prevent external spoofing of withdrawal data.

reachability.notes: JWT authentication prevents external injection. Withdrawal address spoofing requires CL compromise. Withdrawal addresses are determined by validator credentials on the beacon chain.

properties.severity_justification: Spoofed withdrawal addresses would credit ETH to wrong accounts. Impact is detectable on-chain but could be significant if exploited.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Requires CL compromise or JWT bypass. Engine API is not an external-reachable entry point for attackers.

properties.text: Block objects must be immutable after freeze(Block) is called. The header, transactions, ommers, and withdrawals fields must not be modifiable after construction.

reachability.notes: Blocks received via P2P are deserialized and frozen. If freeze can be bypassed, block contents could be mutated between validation and execution.

properties.severity_justification: Block mutation after freeze could allow validated blocks to be modified before execution, causing TOCTOU (time-of-check-time-of-use) vulnerabilities.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate mutation of a frozen Block object between validation and execution.

properties.text: The block's transactions field must only contain objects of type Bytes (for typed transactions) or LegacyTransaction. No other types may be present in the transactions tuple.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends block via P2P containing transaction objects of unexpected types. Deserialization must reject invalid transaction types.

properties.severity_justification: Invalid transaction types in blocks could cause type confusion, incorrect processing, or crashes during transaction execution.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block containing an invalid transaction type being accepted.

properties.text: Receipt objects must be immutable after freeze(Receipt) is called. The succeeded, cumulative_gas_used, bloom, and logs fields must not be modifiable after construction.

reachability.notes: Receipts are constructed internally during transaction execution. Mutation after freeze is an internal-only concern.

properties.severity_justification: Receipt mutation after freeze could alter transaction success status or gas accounting, but requires internal code error.

properties.text: Log objects must be immutable after freeze(Log) is called. The address, topics, and data fields must not be modifiable after construction.

reachability.notes: Logs are constructed during EVM execution. Mutation after freeze is an internal-only concern.

properties.severity_justification: Log mutation would affect bloom filter consistency and event data, but is only possible through internal code error.

properties.text: Log topics tuple must have at most 4 elements, corresponding to LOG0 through LOG4 opcodes. Any log with more than 4 topics must be rejected during EVM execution.

reachability.notes: Attacker deploys a contract that attempts to create logs with more than 4 topics. The EVM should enforce the LOG0-LOG4 limit.

properties.severity_justification: Logs with excessive topics could cause bloom filter computation differences across clients or unexpected behavior in log processing.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate creation of a log with more than 4 topics bypassing EVM validation.

properties.text: The header's base_fee_per_gas must follow the EIP-1559 adjustment rules relative to the parent block's base_fee_per_gas and gas_used. Any deviation must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with incorrect base_fee_per_gas. If the EIP-1559 adjustment is not properly verified, blocks with manipulated base fees could be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect base fee manipulation could allow transactions to pay less than the required fee, effectively enabling fee-free transactions or causing economic instability.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with incorrect base_fee_per_gas being accepted, violating EIP-1559 adjustment rules.

properties.text: The header's blob_gas_used and excess_blob_gas must follow EIP-4844 computation rules relative to the parent block's excess_blob_gas and the number of blobs in the current block. Any deviation must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with incorrect blob gas values. If EIP-4844 computation is not verified, blob fee manipulation is possible.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect blob gas accounting could allow blobs to be submitted without proper fee payment or enable blob gas manipulation attacks.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block with incorrect blob_gas_used or excess_blob_gas being accepted.

properties.text: The header's requests_hash must follow EIP-7685 computation rules. The hash must be computed from the actual system contract requests in the block. Any mismatch must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with incorrect requests_hash. If the hash is not verified against actual system contract requests, tampered requests could be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect requests_hash could allow tampering with system contract requests (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations), affecting validator operations and ETH staking.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with mismatched requests_hash being accepted, enabling system contract request tampering.

properties.text: Blocks received via P2P with an extremely large number of transactions must be rejected early in the validation pipeline, before full deserialization and processing. The block gas_limit and EIP-7934 RLP execution block size limit must serve as upper bounds.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends oversized blocks via P2P containing millions of transactions. Without early size checks, deserialization could exhaust memory.

properties.severity_justification: Oversized blocks can cause memory exhaustion or CPU exhaustion during deserialization, crashing the node. Impact is limited to individual nodes.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a block that exceeds EIP-7934 limits being processed before rejection, causing resource exhaustion.

properties.text: The encode_receipt function must have an explicit error handling path (not relying on implicit fall-through) for transaction types that do not match any known type. If all isinstance checks fail, the function must raise an explicit exception rather than silently returning incorrect data.

reachability.notes: If a new transaction type is added without updating encode_receipt, or if isinstance checks are ambiguous due to class hierarchy, the function may reach an unhandled state.

properties.severity_justification: Missing error handling for unknown transaction types could cause silent incorrect receipt encoding or unhandled exceptions during block processing.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate a transaction type that falls through all isinstance checks without raising an error.

properties.text: The bloom filter bit arithmetic must be deterministic across all implementations: bit_to_set = from_be_bytes(hash[idx:idx+2]) & 0x07FF, bit_index = 0x07FF - bit_to_set, byte_index = bit_index // 8, bit_value = 1 << (7 - (bit_index % 8)). Any implementation deviation in these operations will cause bloom divergence.

reachability.notes: Attacker controls log content which feeds into bloom computation. Different arithmetic implementations across clients would produce different bloom filters for the same logs.

properties.severity_justification: Bloom arithmetic divergence across client implementations causes receipt root mismatch, leading to a network-wide consensus split. Reference stride-007.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must provide test vectors showing different bloom outputs across client implementations for the same input logs.

properties.text: The bloom filter update operation bloom[byte_index] |= bit_value must be an OR operation, not an assignment. Each add_to_bloom call must only set bits, never clear them. The bloom filter must accumulate bits monotonically.

reachability.notes: If a client uses assignment instead of OR, previously set bits would be cleared, producing a different bloom filter.

properties.severity_justification: Using assignment instead of OR in bloom update would clear bits, causing bloom divergence and consensus split.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a client using assignment instead of OR for bloom update, causing different bloom output.

properties.text: Transaction type information is inherently disclosed through the receipt encoding prefix byte. This is by design per EIP-2718 and does not constitute a vulnerability. Receipt data reveals the transaction type (0x01=AccessList, 0x02=FeeMarket, 0x03=Blob, 0x04=SetCode) even without the full transaction.

reachability.notes: Transaction type is publicly visible on-chain. The receipt prefix byte adds no additional information disclosure. This is by design per EIP-2718.

properties.severity_justification: Information disclosed (transaction type) is already publicly available on-chain. No additional mitigation required.

properties.text: The extra_data field in the block header allows up to 32 bytes of arbitrary data set by the block proposer. While this enables covert signaling, block proposer identity is cryptographically linked via CL signature. This is a known feature, not a vulnerability.

reachability.notes: Block proposer sets extra_data. CL signature cryptographically binds the proposer identity. Repudiation is mitigated by design.

properties.severity_justification: Known feature of the block header. Proposer identity is cryptographically linked. Low-severity repudiation concern with no practical exploit.

properties.text: The RLP decoder must enforce resource limits (maximum nesting depth, maximum element count, maximum total decoded size) when processing attacker-controlled data via rlp.decode_to(). Processing deeply nested or extremely large RLP structures must not cause infinite loops, memory exhaustion, or integer overflow.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends receipt bytes with valid prefix but deeply nested or oversized RLP payload. The decode_receipt function passes these bytes directly to the RLP decoder without additional size checks.

properties.severity_justification: RLP decoder resource exhaustion can crash individual nodes. Combined with P2P propagation, this could affect multiple nodes simultaneously.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must demonstrate RLP decoder resource exhaustion (memory or CPU) via crafted receipt bytes.

properties.text: The gas_used field in the block header must not exceed the gas_limit field. For any valid block, header.gas_used <= header.gas_limit must hold. Violation indicates incorrect transaction execution or gas accounting.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with gas_used > gas_limit. If this validation is missing, blocks exceeding gas limits could be accepted.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks with gas_used > gas_limit would break the fundamental gas limit invariant, potentially allowing unbounded computation.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with gas_used exceeding gas_limit being accepted by a client.

properties.text: The bloom filter computation for maximally adversarial inputs (maximum gas block with maximum logs and 4 topics each) must complete within bounded time proportional to the number of log entries. The computation must not exhibit superlinear time complexity.

reachability.notes: Attacker constructs a block maximizing bloom computation cost. Bounded by gas limits and EIP-7825 transaction gas limit cap. This is a known computational cost, not a vulnerability unless superlinear behavior exists.

properties.severity_justification: Bloom computation is O(n) in total log entries, bounded by gas limits. This is a known cost, not an exploitable vulnerability unless the implementation exhibits unexpected complexity.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: Known design limitation. Only eligible if superlinear time complexity can be demonstrated.

properties.text: The header's timestamp must be strictly greater than the parent block's timestamp. A block with timestamp <= parent.timestamp must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with a timestamp equal to or less than the parent. Accepting such blocks could break time-dependent operations and slot calculations.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect timestamp ordering could break EIP-1559 calculations, EIP-4844 blob gas adjustments, and any time-dependent consensus logic.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with non-increasing timestamp being accepted.

properties.text: The header's parent_hash must reference an existing block known to the execution engine. A block with parent_hash pointing to a non-existent or invalid parent must be rejected during validation.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends a block with a fabricated parent_hash. If parent existence is not verified, orphan blocks could corrupt the chain state.

properties.severity_justification: Accepting blocks with invalid parent references could corrupt the execution engine's chain state and fork choice.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with non-existent parent_hash being accepted into the chain.

properties.text: The header bloom filter must equal the OR of all receipt bloom filters in the block: header.bloom == OR(receipt.bloom for all receipts in block). Any discrepancy must cause block rejection.

reachability.notes: Attacker proposes a block with a header bloom that does not match the aggregate of receipt blooms. If unverified, log filtering becomes incorrect.

properties.severity_justification: Incorrect header bloom would affect log query filtering efficiency and correctness, and cause consensus divergence between clients that verify vs. skip this check.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with mismatched header bloom being accepted.

properties.text: The number of withdrawals in a block must not exceed the maximum allowed by the consensus layer (currently 16 per slot). Any block with more than the maximum number of withdrawals must be rejected.

reachability.notes: Attacker sends a block with an excessive number of withdrawals via P2P. The EL must enforce the CL-defined withdrawal count limit.

properties.severity_justification: Excessive withdrawals could cause memory or processing overhead, and if accepted, would credit ETH beyond the CL-authorized amount.
properties.bug_bounty_notes: PoC must show a block with more than 16 withdrawals being accepted by the EL.
